a1.cap: Fewest Arrows to Pop Every Balloon
a1.say: Let's solve Fewest Arrows to Pop Every Balloon, using the Greedy by End approach.

card.title: Fewest Arrows to Pop Every Balloon

a1.cap: Balloons span horizontal ranges [start, end]. An arrow shot straight up at position x pops every balloon with start ≤ x ≤ end. Return the minimum number of arrows that pop all balloons.
a1.say: Balloons span horizontal ranges start, end. An arrow shot straight up at position x pops every balloon with start less than or equal to x less than or equal to end. Return the minimum number of arrows that pop all balloons.

lines: Balloons span horizontal ranges [start, end]. An arrow shot straight up at position x pops every balloon with start ≤ x ≤ end. Return the minimum number of arrows that pop all balloons.

a1.cap: For example, with points = [[10,16],[2,8],[1,6],[7,12]], the answer is 2. Shoot at 6 and 11.
a1.say: For example, with points equals 10, 16, 2, 8, 1, 6, 7, 12, the answer is 2. Shoot at 6 and 11.

a1.cap: Sort balloons by their end. Shoot the first arrow at the end of the earliest-ending balloon; it pops every balloon that starts by then. The next balloon that starts after the arrow needs a new arrow at its own end.
Let's walk through it with points = [[10,16],[2,8],[1,6],[7,12]].
a1.say: Let's walk through it with points equals 10, 16, 2, 8, 1, 6, 7, 12.

a1.cap: [1, 6] isn't popped yet, so shoot arrow 1 at 6.
a1.say: 1, 6 isn't popped yet, so shoot arrow 1 at 6.

a1.cap: [7, 12] isn't popped yet, so shoot arrow 2 at 12.
a1.say: 7, 12 isn't popped yet, so shoot arrow 2 at 12.

a1.cap: Time complexity is O(n log n) and extra space is O(1) extra.
a1.say: Time complexity is O of n log n and extra space is O of one extra.

a1.cap: That's the Greedy by End approach. Now try writing it yourself, in Java or Python!
